content:
Hello! I noticed two things, in Foundation/FirstOrder/Basic/Definability.lean and in Foundation/FirstOrder/SetTheory/Z.lean, and have two related questions.

  1. In Definability.lean, there is an abbrev IsDefinedByWithParam which has this type:
{L : Language} {M : Type u_1} [Structure L M] {k : ℕ}
  (R : (Fin k → M) → Prop) (φ : Semiformula L M k) : Prop

Since φ is a Semiformula L M k, in the case that M is a type which is uncountably infinite, then if I understand Semiformula correctly, it is possible that φ could have uncountably many free variables. When studying definability of a relation R with parameters, is it typical to allow uncountably many free variables in the defining formula?

  1. In Z.lean, there is a lemma separation_exists_eval which takes an argument (φ : SetTheorySemiformula V 1). Here, if V is uncountably infinite, the formula φ may similarly have uncountably many free variables. However, I think φ gets rewritten into ψ, which is a Semiformula ℒₛₑₜ ℕ 1, in order to put ψ in a form where it can be used with the axiom schema of separation. Would it be advisable to try simplifying the proof of separation_exists_eval by only taking arguments φ of type SetTheorySemiformula ℕ 1 instead?

Hi. I think it is a standard treatment of formula with (uncountable) infinite many parameters. And what you’re probably mistaken is, (if I'm not misunderstanding your questions,) that even if there are infinitely many parameters, the number of parameters appearing in each formula is finite.

Specifically, the parameters appearing in a formula is equal to the finite set defined by LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.freeVariables.
